recommendation_summary: For this week's delivery, the reply recommends keeping the shared folder for drafts only. For each release, a reviewer who did not write the document places an unchanged copy in storage that authors cannot change or delete for seven years, with the reviewer's account and the approval time stored alongside it. It rejects the APPROVED initials column and the naming convention as the control. No optional additions are offered. It does not say how the no-self-approval rule would be technically enforced, or which tool or permissions would provide the protected storage.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The signed customer contract requires every released document to keep its exact approved version, the approver's identity, and the approval time for seven years, and it forbids authors approving their own documents or later edits changing that retained version. You asked to keep the shared folder, add an APPROVED column of typed initials, and agree a naming convention for this week's delivery.
labels.Deleted: Typed initials and a naming convention as the release control. They do not freeze the approved bytes, record a trustworthy approver or time, or stop self-approval.
labels.Bottleneck: Authors can still edit the shared folder after a document is marked approved, so the released file is not a retained approved version.
labels.Checked myself: Your statement of the contract, the twelve remote authors, the three reviewers, weekly releases, and author edit access on the current shared folder.

note: The reply recommends author-protected storage for seven years, holding the exact approved copy plus the non-author reviewer's identity and approval time, and its four-line record uses only facts the user supplied.
